ordered_candidate_plan.angle: Southwest cuts its full-year adjusted earnings outlook despite stronger fares, record quarterly revenue and a quarterly earnings beat. Explain how current operating gains and pressure on the next quarter can coexist.
ordered_candidate_plan.evidence_plan: Use only retained goal35-southwest Reuters facts, published 2026-10-21T20:23:00Z, known 2026-10-21T22:27:23.031Z. Attribute issuer guidance through Reuters: 2026 adjusted EPS expected $2.60-$2.85 versus prior $3.25-$4.25; this proves the reported forecasting act, not future achieved earnings. Retain supplied statement that new midpoint is below $2.85 LSEG analyst average without manual midpoint calculation. Bind nearly 27% Q3 average passenger fare increase, Q3 record $8.4bn revenue, higher adjusted operating margin despite fuel costs, fuel bill +$821m year on year, and Q3 adjusted EPS 66 cents versus 58-cent expectation and 11 cents year ago. Final-quarter jet-fuel increase is company expectation only. Do not infer fare increase equals yield, demand or passenger-volume growth; do not calculate fuel sensitivity or attribute entire guidance reduction to fuel. Keep Q3 results and full-year/future expectations separate. Accepted historical 2025 hedge/AOCI case remains dated history; this current report neither independently updates hedge status nor contradicts or invalidates that case. Missing: exact margin, traffic/capacity/mix, fuel-volume/unit-cost split and earnings bridge. Code owns arithmetic. No new retrieval, requests, quotes or media.
ordered_candidate_plan.primary_reader_question: Why can Southwest beat quarterly earnings expectations and raise fares yet cut its full-year profit outlook?
research_queries: Southwest October 21 2026 profit forecast fares fuel costs adjusted earnings
ordered_candidate_plan.selection_rationale: The fresh 2026 guidance change creates an actionable reading question about revenue strength versus earnings exposure, not a recycled hedge-accounting explainer. Concrete reported quarterly gains make a serious countercase to a simple deterioration narrative. Only Southwest selected; prior oil, IBM, Tesla and Meta remain handled.

selection_summary: Select Southwest only: explain the apparent tension between a quarterly beat and lower full-year guidance, with fuel as reported pressure rather than a complete proven earnings bridge. Preserve the accepted historical hedge case.
